architecture_overview.title: Model Architecture & Encoder-Decoder Stack
architecture_overview.summary: The Transformer follows an encoder-decoder architecture using stacked self-attention and point-wise, fully connected layers instead of recurrence or convolutions.
key_points: Encoder: Composed of a stack of N = 6 identical layers. Each layer has two sub-layers: multi-head self-attention and a position-wise fully connected feed-forward network.
Decoder: Composed of a stack of N = 6 identical layers with a third sub-layer that performs multi-head attention over the output of the encoder stack.
Residual Connections: Around each of the sub-layers, employing LayerNorm(x + Sublayer(x)).
Dimensionality: All sub-layers and embedding layers produce outputs of dimension d_model = 512.
Feed-Forward Networks: Inner-layer dimensionality d_ff = 2048 with ReLU activation between two linear transformations: FFN(x) = max(0, x W_1 + b_1) W_2 + b_2.
formulas: FFN(x) = max(0, x W_1 + b_1) W_2 + b_2

scaled_dot_product.title: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
scaled_dot_product.summary: Attention function mapping queries and keys of dimension d_k and values of dimension d_v to an output via scaled dot products and softmax normalization.
key_points: Computes the dot products of the query with all keys, divides each by sqrt(d_k), and applies a softmax function to obtain weights on the values.

Scaling Factor Intuition: For large values of d_k, the dot products grow large in magnitude, pushing the softmax function into regions with extremely small gradients (softmax saturation / vanishing gradient problem). Dividing by sqrt(d_k) counteracts this growth by maintaining unit variance under assumption of independent zero-mean unit-variance components.
Dot-product vs Additive Attention: Dot-product attention is much faster and more space-efficient in practice because it can be implemented using highly optimized matrix multiplication code.
formulas: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax((Q * K^T) / sqrt(d_k)) * V

multi_head_attention.title: Multi-Head Attention
multi_head_attention.summary: Instead of performing a single attention function with d_model-dimensional keys, values and queries, linearly projects queries, keys and values h times with different learned linear projections to d_k, d_k and d_v dimensions respectively.
key_points: Allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions. A single attention head averages these subspaces, inhibiting this capability.
Total computational cost is similar to single-head attention with full dimensionality because d_k = d_v = d_model / h = 64 with h = 8.

Three distinct attention usages: (1) Encoder self-attention where Q, K, V come from previous layer; (2) Decoder self-attention where each position can only attend to earlier positions (masked attention); (3) Decoder-encoder cross-attention where Q comes from decoder and K, V come from encoder.
formulas: MultiHead(Q, K, V) = Concat(head_1, ..., head_h) * W^O
where head_i = Attention(Q * W_i^Q, K * W_i^K, V * W_i^V)
Projection dimensions: W_i^Q in R^(d_model x d_k), W_i^K in R^(d_model x d_k), W_i^V in R^(d_model x d_v), W^O in R^(h*d_v x d_model)

positional_encoding.title: Positional Encoding
positional_encoding.summary: In order for the model to make use of sequence order without recurrence or convolution, positional encodings are injected into the input embeddings.
key_points: Added to input embeddings at the bottoms of encoder and decoder stacks, having the same dimension d_model = 512 so the two can be summed.
Uses sine and cosine functions of different frequencies: wavelengths form a geometric progression from 2*pi to 10000*2*pi.

Mathematical Intuition: For any fixed offset k, PE_(pos+k) can be represented as a linear function of PE_pos using trigonometric angle sum identities: cos(a+b) = cos(a)cos(b) - sin(a)sin(b) and sin(a+b) = sin(a)cos(b) + cos(a)sin(b). This facilitates learning relative positions.
Extrapolation: The authors chose sinusoidal encodings because it may allow the model to extrapolate to sequence lengths longer than those encountered during training.
formulas: where pos is token position and i is the dimension index (0 <= i < d_model/2)

computational_complexity.title: Self-Attention vs Recurrent and Convolutional Layers
computational_complexity.summary: Comparison of self-attention layers to recurrent and convolutional layers across total computational complexity per layer, parallelizability, and path length for long-range dependencies.
key_points: Self-Attention: Complexity per layer is O(n^2 * d), sequential operations O(1), maximum path length O(1).
Recurrent Layer: Complexity per layer is O(n * d^2), sequential operations O(n), maximum path length O(n).
Convolutional Layer: Complexity per layer is O(k * n * d^2), sequential operations O(1), maximum path length O(log_k(n)) with dilated convolutions.

Key trade-off: When sequence length n is smaller than representation dimension d (common in NLP tasks where e.g. n=512, d=512 or d=1024), self-attention layer is computationally faster than recurrent layers.
Path length: Shorter path length O(1) makes it much easier to learn long-range dependencies because gradient signals do not need to traverse numerous sequential steps.
formulas: Table 1 Comparison: Layer Type | Complexity per Layer | Sequential Operations | Maximum Path Length
Convolutional:     O(k * n * d^2) | O(1) | O(log_k(n))
